grounding.quote: "description": "URI-reference syntax annotation. Conformance requires an assertion-capable URI-reference validator in addition to portable Draft 2020-12 structural validation."

constraints.statement: identityUri is a nonempty string annotated uri; referenceUri is a nonempty string annotated uri-reference. Conformance additionally requires assertion-capable validators for both formats. references is a unique array of referenceUri permitting empty; nonEmptyReferences additionally requires at least one item. sha256 is a string matching ^[0-9a-f]{64}$. stdoChannelUri intersects identityUri with ^stdo://channels/(?![^/]*-rc\.)[0-9A-Za-z][0-9A-Za-z._+-]*/?$. stdoReleaseUri intersects identityUri with ^stdo://releases/v[0-9A-Za-z][0-9A-Za-z._+-]*-rc\.[1-9][0-9]*/?$. These distinct patterns permit optional terminal slash and require a positive, non-zero-leading RC number for a release.

grounding.quote: "description": "Mutable version-line discovery selector carried by an annotated Git tag. It is never operative constitutional authority without digest-bound explicit resolution and adoption."
"description": "Reading route relative to the referenced constitutional basis."

constraints.statement: stdoBinding requires source, selector and basis. Source requires repository: referenceUri identifying the Git repository carrying the selected release line and immutable RC cuts. Selector is stdoChannelUri and is never operative constitutional authority without digest-bound explicit resolution and adoption. Basis requires uri: stdoReleaseUri identifying the exact immutable installed cut and manifest_sha256: sha256 identifying its deterministic installed-release manifest. constitutionalEntrypoint requires basis and uri, both referenceUri; its reading URI resolves relative to the referenced constitutional basis. These objects disallow additional properties.

conditions: Before constitutional work in the scope routed by each respective bootstrap template.

grounding.quote:
1. Resolve the applicable `stdo_<label>.json` for the requested Product scope.
2. Use `constitution.stdo.basis`, not its mutable selector, as the operative basis.
3. Resolve and verify that exact installed release through the STDO toolchain manager.
4. Load the Product Definition's declared bootstrap entrypoint, then exact owning standards as needed.
5. Resolve the applicable accepted Project Reference-Frame Basis or its declared composition.
6. Bind the exact outcome, basis and existing work grant. Use direct Writer entry when the accepted frame configuration permits it and one capable context suffices; use Executive or the declared project equivalent for material coordination. Activate only applicable dependency-ready evaluations, preserving unknown applicability and required independence. Executive does not mutate files or Git; a separate Writer activation binds those effects.
7. Fail closed when the Product Definition, frame basis, subject, authority, or activation is missing, ambiguous, stale, or outside the governed scope.

6. Bind the exact outcome, basis and existing work grant. Use direct Writer entry when the accepted frame configuration permits it and one capable context suffices; use Executive or the declared project equivalent for material coordination. Activate only applicable dependency-ready evaluations, preserving unknown applicability and required independence. Executive does not mutate files or Git; a separate Writer activation binds those effects.
7. Fail closed when the Product Definition, frame basis, subject, authority, or activation is missing, ambiguous, stale, or outside the governed scope.

constraints.statement: Each template prescribes the same ordered prework: resolve the applicable scoped stdo_<label>.json; use constitution.stdo.basis rather than selector; resolve and verify that exact installed release through the manager; load the declared bootstrap entrypoint then exact owning standards as needed; resolve the applicable accepted frame basis or declared composition; bind exact outcome, basis and existing work grant. Direct Writer entry requires both accepted-configuration permission and one sufficient capable context; material coordination uses Executive or the declared equivalent. Only applicable dependency-ready evaluations may activate, with unknown applicability and required independence preserved. Executive cannot mutate files or Git; those effects require separate Writer activation. Missing, ambiguous, stale or out-of-scope Product Definition, frame basis, subject, authority or activation causes fail-closed behavior.
constraints.uncertainty: This records the two templates' prescribed workflow without performing it or supplying missing admission law.

Reviewer grades severity and returns evidence, affected claims, causal
assessment where supportable, blast radius, workaround, repair complexity,
regression risk, confidence, and residual uncertainty. Under the executive
profile, Executive assigns priority and determines promotion-boundary effect against the complete Product
view and current mandate. Severity, priority, frame result, boundary effect,

and `P0..Pn`, including a `P2` decision cutoff, only by defining their exact
direction and effect here. When a finding blocks promotion, and that a
cutoff cannot waive a hard stop or turn an out-of-claim observation into a

promotion.

conditions: Entry, coordination or continuation of represented constructive work.
exceptions: Executive-specific steps apply only under the adopted Executive profile.

grounding.quote:
Bind the sufficient direct Writer path and the material conditions requiring
coordination under the selected law. Direct entry still needs exact work
authority, admission, operation scope and closure conditions. It does not add
a ticket, coordinating appointment or review when none is applicable.

For coordinated work:

```text
existing authority
  -> Executive basis and outcome lock
  -> exact Worker, Reviewer, or specialist activation
  -> closed result and Reviewer technical triage where applicable
  -> Executive or declared conjunction
  -> Executive priority and boundary effect
  -> authorized disposition and next activation | stop | re-entry

No child result, tool output, model response, shared actor, or lateral handoff
activates another frame or authorizes continuation by itself
(`ACTIVATION.md` section 1, Admission).

Executive performs no file or Git mutation. The same actor may construct only
after entering a separately bound Writer activation with the inherited exact
grant. Changing roles does not create authority or independent assessment.

constraints.statement: Bind a sufficient direct Writer path and material conditions requiring coordination. Direct entry requires exact work authority, admission, operation scope and closure conditions, without adding an inapplicable ticket, coordinating appointment or review. Coordinated topology is existing authority → basis/outcome lock → exact Worker/Reviewer/specialist activation → closed result plus applicable Reviewer triage → Executive or declared conjunction → priority/boundary effect → authorized disposition and next activation, stop or re-entry. Child results, tool outputs, model responses, shared actors and lateral handoffs cannot alone activate another frame or authorize continuation. Executive makes no file/Git mutation. Construction by the same actor requires separately bound Writer activation inheriting the exact grant; changing role creates neither authority nor independence.
constraints.uncertainty: Topology is represented as source-described order, not an executed traversal.

conditions: Coverage accounting, result reuse or closure of an exact claim.

grounding.quote:
Coverage is complete only when every mandatory material evaluation and
interaction is closed, or governing authority explicitly retains its residual
consistently with the claim (`REFERENCE_FRAME.md` section 8, Operational full
coverage). Record each material row's status in the values of that section's
Coverage ledger. A `residual` row is
`excluded_by_authority` where governing authority explicitly retains its
residual consistently with the claim, and otherwise `conditionally_covered` or
`uncovered`. A `non_material` row is no material evaluation and takes no
coverage status; its non-material evidence stays in the inventory above.
Available frame count and coordinator visibility are not coverage.

Reuse a valid result after checking its question, subject/basis, evidence and
invalidators. Record reusable judgments and original owner rulings through the
existing work carrier under TICKETS, separately from interpretation.
Changed material premises invalidate affected claims under the invalidators
of `ACTIVATION.md` section 7; a new role or session alone does not. Required independent assessments still supply their own
judgment. Closure requires satisfied applicable obligations, valid evidence,
required judgments/rulings and no active non-closure condition; review is not
itself the closing event.

constraints.statement: Record exact coverage tuple/evaluation interval; each material evaluation's capable activation or residual; interactions/Product-edge coverage; intentional overlap/independence; uncovered, conditional, conflicted, unknown, excluded and out-of-frame residuals; and exact-claim terminal closure predicate. Completeness requires every mandatory material evaluation and interaction closed or its residual explicitly retained by governing authority consistently with the claim. Use the cited Coverage ledger values: residual is excluded_by_authority only with that retention, otherwise conditionally_covered or uncovered. non_material takes no coverage status; retain its evidence in inventory. Frame count and coordinator visibility do not establish coverage. Reuse valid results only after checking question, subject/basis, evidence and invalidators; record reusable judgments/original owner rulings in the existing TICKETS work carrier separately from interpretation. Changed material premises invalidate affected claims; a new role/session alone does not. Required independent assessments supply their own judgments. Closure requires satisfied applicable obligations, valid evidence, required judgments/rulings and no active non-closure condition; review alone is not closure.
constraints.uncertainty: The full coverage ledger, invalidators and work-carrier law are referenced but not supplied.

conditions: Before activation and disposition, and when material inputs or basis change.

grounding.quote:
Revalidate before activation and disposition:

- outcome lock: Goal, Product outcome, current MVP or release mandate,
  promotion policy, boundary, and re-entry class;
- basis lock: subject, checkpoint, authority, dependency, configuration,
  topology, evidence, and time;
- Product-role lock: Source Project, Product Definition, Development Product,
  Release Cut, Product, Install, Artifact, and dependency roles;
- authority lock: semantic, evaluation, operation, decision, acceptance, and
  publication owners and grants; and
- coverage-and-return lock: material evaluations, interactions, residuals, and
  declared result routes.

Exact review checkpoints and released Products remain immutable under their
own lifecycle law. Their immutability does not make the Source Project building
a successor immutable. A lawful mutation creates a new checkpoint and
invalidates every affected prior result.

constraints.statement: Before activation and disposition revalidate outcome lock (Goal, Product outcome, current MVP/release mandate, promotion policy, boundary, re-entry class), basis lock (subject, checkpoint, authority, dependency, configuration, topology, evidence, time), Product-role lock (Source Project, Product Definition, Development Product, Release Cut, Product, Install, Artifact, dependency roles), authority lock (semantic, evaluation, operation, decision, acceptance, publication owners/grants), and coverage/return lock (material evaluations, interactions, residuals, result routes). List every invalidating method, Product, outcome, subject, checkpoint, candidate, dependency, composition-contract, actor, capability, evidence, authority, workspace or topology change as a named material-input/basis change affecting the basis or derived activations/results/conjunctions/coverage. Exact review checkpoints and released Products remain immutable under their lifecycle law; this does not freeze a successor-building Source Project. Lawful mutation creates a new checkpoint and invalidates every affected prior result.

conditions: Filling a per-product overlay.

grounding.quote:
One definition represents one distinct product `WHAT`. Put multiple
independent realizations of that same `WHAT` in `how.build_tenants`, not in
additional definition files.

`reference_frame_bases` is required and non-empty. Point each `uri` at the
accepted project frame-basis declaration already carried by Product,
requirements, local constitutional authority, accepted design, or another
lawful surface. Bind every admitting authority and exact governed scope. The
default path uses `./specification/REFERENCE_FRAME_BASIS.md`; replace it when
the owning project chooses another layout. Do not put agent identities or
temporary frame activations in the Product Definition Overlay; their authorized
work instruction or activation packet cites the applicable basis.

Set `product.bounded_context` to `null` when the product does not claim a
separate enclosing bounded context. The field is not an exhaustive registry;
subordinate, peer, composed, tenant, user, and runtime contexts remain in their
own authority and are related explicitly. Remove the illustrative
disambiguation when it does not apply. Empty local-constitution and composition
arrays are explicit declarations of none.

constraints.statement: One overlay defines one distinct WHAT; multiple independent realizations belong in how.build_tenants. Agent identities and temporary activations belong in authorized instructions/packets citing the basis, not the overlay. Replace disambiguation for every material local resolution, or remove the example and retain empty when none; bind complete candidates/selected concept/carrier/authority/bases/context/scope. Cross-context meaning stays in the owning carrier. Use bounded_context null when no separate enclosing context is claimed; other contexts retain their authorities and explicit relations. assertion-capable RFC 3986 validator for the annotated URI and URI-reference
formats, then resolve every URI and fragment, verify the selected immutable
constitutional set, confirm unique definition and tenant identities, verify

conditions: Use of the described toolchain operations on filled definitions.

grounding.quote:
For a filled definition, `stdo sync --definition <file>` installs and verifies
only its already selected exact basis. Run
`stdo adopt --definition <file> --dry-run` to show the immutable cut currently
advertised by its annotated version-line selector and its exact plan digest;
apply with `--accept-plan-sha256 <digest>` in a separate invocation only after
explicitly accepting that basis change. `stdo bootstrap --definition <file>`
preflights targets relative to `product.source_project` and refreshes only the
declared marker-bounded agent bootstrap. Fleet writes require `--all`; fleet
adoption also requires its separately presented aggregate plan digest.

constraints.statement: The schema URI uses the same exact logical release basis, contains no machine-local store path, and is resolved through the manager after installing the cut once; project-local .genesis is not required. Described sync installs/verifies only the already selected basis. Adopt dry-run displays the selector-advertised immutable cut and exact plan digest; applying requires a separate invocation with --accept-plan-sha256 <digest> after explicit acceptance of that basis change. Bootstrap preflights targets relative to source_project and refreshes only declared marker-bounded bootstrap content. Fleet writes require --all; fleet adoption additionally requires the separately presented aggregate plan digest.
constraints.uncertainty: Commands are interpreted as source-described operations and are not executed.

ADR conventions and frontmatter shape are defined in `SPEC_METHOD.md` section 10, Design records. See `design/adrs/README.md` for the full conventions and `design/adrs/ADR_TEMPLATE.md` for the canonical ADR shape.

One ADR per decision boundary, not per requirement file. Cross-tenant scope is the constraint that distinguishes this folder from a tenant-local one: the decision must govern more than one tenant. If scope narrows during implementation, move to the relevant tenant and record the move in the supersession chain.
